title: BLTDistill patch loss div factor used input_ids.numel() — wrong scaling for byte-level losses
root_cause: The byte-level loss div factor was computed as loss_div_factor / input_ids.numel(), but loss_div_factor passed in is at the byte sequence level not the patch level. The correct denominator is h_byte.shape[0] * h_byte.shape[1] (number of byte positions), and the patch loss needs an analogous division by patch positions. The mismatch silently mis-weighted byte vs patch loss components.
invariant: Each loss component must be divided by the number of valid positions of that component's granularity (bytes vs patches), not by input_ids.numel().
diff_summary: Divide loss_div_factor by h_byte.shape[0]*h_byte.shape[1] for the byte loss, and patch_loss_div_factor by h_patch.shape[0]*h_patch.shape[1] for the patch loss.
silent_check: Forward and backward run normally — losses are finite, just mis-scaled relative to each other; the model trains but with a silently shifted balance between byte and patch objectives.
